issues: Finding citing doi-10-1016-j-ipm-2026-104709 slightly overstates the accessible evidence by saying multi-source fact verification 'benefits ... from retaining different evidence-source roles'. The analysis establishes that HeterMV explicitly preserves source roles and reports better benchmark results, and says ablations validate major components, but the abstract/preview-level evidence supplied does not isolate preservation of source roles as the causal source of the gain.

The contradiction entry 'Single document-level factuality versus preservation of source- or mention-relative assessments' is better described as a representational/task-definition tension than a contradiction. doi-10-1007-s11390-024-2655-1 collapses differing local factualities into one document-level prediction, while doi-10-1007-s10579-009-9089-9 and doi-10-18653-v1-2023-findings-acl-44 model source-relative factuality; these choices are not logically incompatible and can coexist in a richer model.

The finding on correction and retraction is mostly faithful, but the clause that both are changes to current commitments 'rather than erasure of earlier utterances' is directly established for retraction by doi-10-1023-a-1010318403544. doi-10-1093-jos-ffn013 supports persistence, removal of disavowed commitments, and restoration after correction-of-correction, but does not in the supplied analysis explicitly formulate correction as preservation of a historical utterance record.
unsupported_claims: The phrase 'benefits ... from retaining different evidence-source roles' for doi-10-1016-j-ipm-2026-104709 is stronger than the supplied preview-level analysis supports as a component-specific causal conclusion.
Treating document-level factuality and source-relative factuality as a contradiction overstates what is actually a difference in representation and task scope.
notes: All cited paper_ids are in the permitted set, and the synthesis is broadly faithful to the supplied analyses. The major component-level conclusions on source-relative factuality, temporal ordering, commitment lifecycles, correction/retraction, belief change, temporal history, provenance, and event sourcing are traceable to the analyses. The synthesis appropriately preserves the empirical tension over transitivity between doi-10-1162-tacl-a-00182 and 1909.05360 and the dataset-dependent reversal within doi-10-18653-v1-d18-1155 rather than averaging them into universal claims. It also correctly reports the internal parameter-count inconsistency in doi-10-1016-j-ipm-2021-102836. All eight gaps remain explicitly open, and none is falsely presented as resolved. Transfer-domain boundaries are handled well: news-derived NLP, formal dialogue and belief-revision work, database theory, event-sourcing practice, and adjacent fact verification are not presented as direct validation of longitudinal workplace communication. The actionable insights are clearly labeled as synthesis-derived project recommendations rather than experimentally established production claims. The identified issues are wording/classification problems rather than failures that undermine the overall synthesis.
